name: The Agent builds the page, the designer still nudges the pixels
object: Framer Agents, shown building a full homepage from a one-line prompt while the designer keeps hand-level control over layout, position and custom code
audience: designers who want AI speed for the first draft but still want to hand-tune spacing, components and code themselves
message: This video tells designers that the Framer Agent gets you to a real homepage in one prompt, then gets out of the way so you can still adjust every pixel by hand.

moments.what: a New Chat panel takes a single prompt for a homepage for an AI well-being research lab called Bloom, typed live
moments.copy: Create a sleek black homepage for an AI well-being research lab called Bloom.

moments.what: the Agent narrates its own plan in the chat, then builds the page structure live on canvas; the designer switches to the Style tab and nudges a block's Position values by hand
moments.copy: I'll now build the page structure from scratch on the target page, keeping it editable and matching the reference's spacing, typography and surfaces.

moments.what: cuts to a custom code component, ImageWheel.tsx, open in an editor beside its live draggable preview, and a CMS table of team member rows with photos and status
a finished brand page is shown across desktop, tablet and mobile previews side by side, then closes on framer.com and the Framer glyph
moments.copy: We build the tools that make intelligence feel creative.

cta: no explicit spoken call to action; closes on the framer.com wordmark beside the Framer glyph after the responsive preview
why: Cutting from a one-line prompt straight to the designer manually nudging a position value proves the promise in the title, design with AI, keep control, instead of just asserting it.
